judges.policy.chosen_on: thresholds and rule: calibration half of data/scribe/v3/judges/pairs-v1.jsonl; the v2 question set was designed after the v1 results of both halves had been seen (see question_sets.disclosure in the benchmark)

audit.sampling.note: the two statuses were sampled at very different rates, so pooled_unweighted is NOT a rate for the round-2 dataset; quote by_status

student.multiplicity: Holm over the 3 pre-registered comparisons that were run (pooled endpoint)
student.decoding: unconstrained greedy, tolerant parsing (the frozen version-2 setting)
student.V3-270m-nemotron.what: primary: + round-2 notes accepted by the Jev gate
student.V3-270m-all.what: secondary: + round-2 notes + version-2 Haiku notes
student.C-270m-all-v2data.what: secondary: version-2 data with the Haiku notes
student.S-1b-lora-r16.what: size ladder, Gemma 3 1B: evaluated on test because it beat the reference on validation (pre-registered rule p < 0.05)
cascade.student_choice_reason: highest validation exact match is C-270m-all-v2data (134/310); the pre-registered primary V3-270m-nemotron (124/310) and it lie within each other's Wilson 95% intervals, so the rule prefers the primary
cascade.threshold_rule: on validation notes only: accept a note when its score >= t; t is the value with the largest validation coverage whose observed error among accepted notes is <= the target, with at least 20 accepted notes; otherwise no threshold is set
cascade.empirical_not_guaranteed: the thresholds are chosen on 310 synthetic validation notes (the subset ones on fewer); the error on new notes can be higher
cascade.verdict: 5% target, all 700 test notes: adding Jev did not let measurably more notes skip review: every coverage difference is within noise. Skip review: student confidence alone 270/700 (38.6%), Jev alone 263/700 (37.6%), student + Jev 276/700 (39.4%). Coverage difference vs the student: Jev -1.0 points (test bootstrap 95% -3.1 to +1.1 points; with threshold re-choice -4.9 to +6.9 points), student + Jev +0.9 points (-0.9 to +2.7 points; -4.4 to +7.3 points).

5% target, error among the notes that skipped review (pooled test): student 28/270 (10.4%), Jev 7/263 (2.7%), student + Jev 12/276 (4.3%). Difference vs the student, Jev: -11.0 to -4.5 points on these test notes (lower, outside noise), -10.8 to +1.5 points with threshold re-choice (within noise); student + Jev: -9.0 to -3.5 points (lower, outside noise), -10.3 to +1.2 points (within noise). The observed pooled test error was at or below the target for: Jev alone, student + Jev (logistic); above it for: student confidence alone. Haiku-written test notes: student 21/61 (34.4%), Jev 3/55 (5.5%), student + Jev 8/65 (12.3%) wrong among skipped; Nemotron-written: 7/209 (3.4%), 4/208 (1.9%), 4/211 (1.9%).

10% target, all 700 test notes: adding Jev let more notes skip review on these test notes (outside test-sampling noise), but the gain is within noise once the thresholds are re-chosen on resampled validation notes. Skip review: student confidence alone 287/700 (41.0%), Jev alone 309/700 (44.1%), student + Jev 315/700 (45.0%). Coverage difference vs the student: Jev +3.1 points (test bootstrap 95% +1.1 to +5.1 points; with threshold re-choice -2.4 to +6.7 points), student + Jev +4.0 points (+2.3 to +5.7 points; -0.9 to +6.0 points).

10% target, error among the notes that skipped review (pooled test): student 36/287 (12.5%), Jev 43/309 (13.9%), student + Jev 48/315 (15.2%). Difference vs the student, Jev: -1.9 to +4.8 points on these test notes (within noise), -8.5 to +7.1 points with threshold re-choice (within noise); student + Jev: +0.3 to +5.3 points (higher, outside noise), -6.2 to +6.0 points (within noise). The observed pooled test error was at or below the target for: none; above it for: student confidence alone, Jev alone, student + Jev (logistic). Haiku-written test notes: student 28/73 (38.4%), Jev 30/87 (34.5%), student + Jev 34/92 (37.0%) wrong among skipped; Nemotron-written: 8/214 (3.7%), 13/222 (5.9%), 14/223 (6.3%).

Ranking over all coverage levels (area under the risk-coverage curve, pooled test, lower is better): student 0.2689, Jev 0.2545 (difference -0.0144, paired bootstrap 95% -0.0210 to -0.0083), student + Jev 0.2529 (-0.0159; -0.0221 to -0.0101); random order 0.6186, best possible order 0.2514.

Decisions, on the 93 hash-chosen test notes of the subset (thresholds from 93 validation notes): at 5% Decisions alone 23/93 (24.7%) vs student 41/93 (44.1%) (difference -28.0 to -10.8 points), three-way 33/93 (35.5%) vs student + Jev 41/93 (44.1%); at 10% Decisions alone 32/93 (34.4%) vs student 44/93 (47.3%) (difference -20.4 to -5.4 points), three-way 43/93 (46.2%) vs student + Jev 44/93 (47.3%). AURC there: student 0.2297, Decisions 0.2647, student + Jev 0.2216, three-way 0.2223.

_docs.judges.report160.*: pairs that both judges answered (80 corrupted, 80 clean). false_reject is measured on notes the version-2 Jev gate had already accepted, so it is biased low; see scribe/judges/RESULTS.md
_docs.judges.report300.jev_hint.*: the v2 question set was designed after both halves' v1 results were seen: not a clean hold-out
_docs.audit.*: auditors were language-model readers (Claude Haiku) who saw the claimed labels; accepted and rejected were sampled at different rates, so do not pool
_docs.student.*: every run used the same 324 optimisation steps (train_steps), so a run with more training rows (train_examples) made fewer passes over each note; compare data arms with that in mind. v3_vs_v2_* keys are the pre-registered primary against the frozen version-2 reference
_docs.cascade.*: thresholds chosen on validation notes only and applied to test; empirical, not guarantees. *95 keys are paired bootstrap 95% intervals; 'pipeline' intervals also re-choose the thresholds on resampled validation notes. Decisions keys are on a hash-chosen subset only. Synthetic notes; not for clinical use

_format: flat keys; shares are <key>.n, <key>.d, <key>.share (+ .wilson95); null values are explained in _not_done; sources in _sources
